narrative:
The model estimates a 69% chance that you will leave your job, which is why your promotion request has been denied. This prediction is driven primarily by three key factors in your profile.

Your relatively short overall work experience of 1-5 years was the strongest influence pulling the prediction toward leaving. Among employees the model expects to stay, only about half have this same low level of experience, while the rest tend to have six or more years. This limited background appears to signal higher turnover risk to the system.

The second most important factor was that you have received other job offers while working here. This strongly pushed the prediction toward you leaving, as external opportunities often indicate that someone is considering or actively exploring exits.

Third, working in the “other” sector also contributed toward predicting departure. This sector shows a noticeably lower retention rate compared with medical or education fields, where far more employees are predicted to stay.

Although several positive elements exist in your profile, such as receiving a bonus, having no overtime, and reporting an easy work-life balance, these were not enough to outweigh the top three influences.

The organization should consider discussing your career goals with you directly and exploring ways to accelerate your development and experience within the company. You may want to reflect on whether the external opportunities you’ve received better align with your long-term plans. Addressing these areas could improve both your trajectory and future promotion prospects.
